newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - United Utils profits set to surge.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - United Utils profits set to surge.

text.p: Half year profits at Britain's United Utilities, formed last year when North West Water bought electricity firm NORWEB, should show gains on November 28 and analysts will look for more evidence of merger benefits.

Half year pretax profits are expected to rise to between 220 and 249 million stg from 167 million stg a year ago and the dividend payout could be anywhere between 10.6 and 12.5 pence per share, up from 9.3 pence previously.
"United have guaranteed 11 percent real dividend increases and they have said more if it is possible. I think they will be aggressive on the increase," said one analyst.
United Utilities was the first multi-utility to be formed and promised cost savings of 105 million stg in 1997/98, but some analysts felt part of these savings had been targeted before the merger.
But productivity gains from its joint services company Vertex should show through in half year results, analysts said, and the company may announce new initiatives for the unit.

Hyder, a multi-utility created when Welsh Water took over South Wales Electricity (Swalec) at the start of the year, said on Friday that the electricity company should be materially earnings enhancing on a full year basis.
United might also give an update on planned sales of non-core activities, analysts said.

On November 4 it sold the loan portfolio of its NORWEB Retail unit for 100 million stg to Lombard Tricity Finance Ltd, bringing the total revenue from sales to 238 million stg out of a target 350 million stg.
It sold its NORWEB Retail business to the Comet Group, part of Kingfisher, for a net 22 million stg on November 12.
